chapters.1: Paul opens with praise for the spiritual blessings believers receive in Christ, including being chosen, adopted, and redeemed according to God's eternal plan. He prays that the Ephesians would grasp the hope of their calling and the immense power God demonstrated in raising Christ and placing him as head over the church.
chapters.2: Paul reminds the Ephesians that they were once spiritually dead because of sin but have been made alive through God's grace, not through any effort of their own. He explains that Christ has broken down the division between Jews and Gentiles, uniting both groups into one new community built together as God's dwelling place.
chapters.3: Paul describes his special calling to reveal the 'mystery' that Gentiles are now full partners with Jews in God's family through the gospel. He prays that the Ephesians would be strengthened inwardly and come to grasp the vast, surpassing love of Christ.
chapters.4: Paul urges believers to maintain unity while using their different spiritual gifts to build up the church toward maturity in Christ. He calls them to leave behind their old sinful way of life and put on a new character marked by truthfulness, kindness, and forgiveness instead of anger and bitterness.
chapters.5: Paul calls believers to imitate God's love and avoid behaviors like sexual immorality, greed, and foolish talk that belong to darkness rather than light. He then addresses household relationships, calling husbands and wives to mutual love and respect, comparing the marriage relationship to Christ's sacrificial love for the church.
chapters.6: Paul gives instructions for children, parents, servants, and masters to treat each other rightly out of respect for Christ. He closes with the well-known image of the 'armor of God,' describing truth, righteousness, faith, and prayer as spiritual equipment for standing firm against evil.
